findings.reason: without §29 in the open followup the section's only route into a dispatch is a coordinator noticing it outside the plan's own chain, and the stale in-flight claims send work at sections the plan says are closed.
findings.text: f-wftl-007 is the plan's only open followup and its title and body name §9, §22, §24, §26, §27 and §28, while this version's declarations mark s24, s26, s27 and s28 done and add s29 as implementable; a coordinator driving the plan from its open followup dispatches four landed sections and never dispatches §29

findings.reason: the case is one assertion in a test the section already creates, and without it the section's own gate cannot distinguish an attempt-scoped retirement from a blanket one.
findings.text: s29's deliverable says "the run's live pointer is retired and its worktree released" and its first case ends in no live pointer, but no case plants a live pointer written by a newer attempt on the same run; the finish path deliberately preserves such a pointer because removing it strands an attempt still in flight (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:499-509, and _release_marked_pointer's attempt comparison), so an implementation that retires whatever pointer is live — the naive reading of the deliverable — passes all three cases and the negative control

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the four landing commits the closure notes cite (6f4c45605d, ec87744c09, b2f102aadc, d3eef3d59e) are commits in the repository, s29's write path reckon/crew/pending_landing.py exists, tests/test_a_finished_pending_landing_retires_its_run.py is new, and the cross-plan sections s29's Why cites (a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker §29, a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan §41) resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s29's done-when proves the retirement happens for the pass's own attempt, but plants no live pointer belonging to a newer attempt, so an implementation that retires whatever pointer is live passes every case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the four closure notes added in this change link to anchors (#s24-split-dispatch, #s26-measured-arm-reads-its-receipt, #s27-lander-never-waits-on-a-measurement, #s28-acceptance-check-holds-no-lease) that resolve under docs/evidence/archive/work-flows-to-the-lane-landed.html, and s29 names the section's evidence fragment on that same durable path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s29 names no plan label in a symbol, filename or comment; the plan references in its Why sit in plan prose, where plan-to-plan citation belongs, and the new test's name reads as the behaviour.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — s29's root cause matches the code it writes to: the finish path retires only a pointer carrying pending_landing_repair and skips an unmarked live pointer outright (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:423, 499-509), and commit 6f4c45605d shows the pass itself finishing a promoted landing with the run's pointer left behind, which is the stated defect; the endpoint is checkable and the negative control can fail.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s29 states one deliverable, retiring a run whose pending landing the pass has just finished, in three cases of one behaviour.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — f-wftl-007, the plan's only open followup, names §9, §22, §24, §26, §27 and §28 while s29 is newly declared implementable at plan.html:23 and is named by no followup, and the same followup still describes §24, §27 and §28 as in flight after their closure notes record them landed.
